newsitem.title: USA: NFL-BRUNELL WILL MISS EIGHT WEEKS.
newsitem.headline: NFL-BRUNELL WILL MISS EIGHT WEEKS.

text.p: Arthroscopic surgery Thursday revealed no tear in the ligament in Mark Brunell's right knee, and his doctor said the Jacksonville Jaguar quarterback will miss eight weeks of the season.

"When we looked in there, the (ligament) was damaged," Dr. Stephen Lucie said. "We could tell that it stretched out a bit, we could see some damage to the ligament. He had an old tear to that area, so again, this complicates our exam. But what we found was some partial tearing of that ligament."

Jacksonville supporters complained when the schedule makers gave the team an open date the weekend of September 14th, but now it appears to be an huge break, since Brunell -- who last season was the first quarterback in 33 years to lead his position in passing and rushing yardage -- should miss just five or six games.
Brunell, who signed a five-year, $31 million contract last month, was hit by New York Giants linebacker Jessie Armstead after throwing a pass in a preseason game Saturday night at Giants Stadium.
The 26-year-old Brunell injured the same knee in 1991 while playing for the University of Washington. He underwent ligament reconstruction repair at that time.

Brunell rose to prominence last year when he led the Jaguars to the AFC Championship. Jacksonville upset Buffalo in the wild-card round and then knocked off Denver, the top team in the AFC during the regular season, in the divisional playoff before losing to New England.
He became the first quarterback since Johnny Unitas in 1963 to lead the league in passing yards (4,367) and pace all quarterbacks in rushing yards (400).
